messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging SRE oncall: streaming.tail_latency.p99 alert for tenant 'heliospay' on pool 'eu-west-2-tenant-17' — p99=12.4s (SLO=3s). Active 11:03:18 UTC. Link: https://monitoring.redwood/alerts/1733332222

sasha.ng: saw the alert. customer is single-tenant Dedicated. They sent a weird prompt batch around the spike window. grabbing logs now.

kai.chen: can you dump a few example prompts? suspecting prompt-based KVCACHE thrash.

sasha.ng: example (sanitized):
```
USER_PROMPT:\n"START_DELIM<<<***USER_START***>>>PROMPT_BODY
<lots of repeated '---' blocks and many unusual delimiter tokens>
END_DELIM"
```
These are long streaming requests with repeated delimiter sequences. We get repeated KV cache invalidations and OOM-ish long lookups.

eng-sre-oncall: corroborating — tail logs show long step times in the runtime with repeated cache misses. snippet from runtime trace (structured):
```
[11:03:19.123] req=rc-9a1f kv_cache_hit=false seq_len=4096 tokens=620 compute_ms=8100 stage=kv_lookup
[11:03:19.125] req=rc-9a1f stage=attention compute_ms=2300 memory_mb=14200
[11:03:20.451] req=rc-9a1f overall_ms=10400 p99_bucket
```
We also see a high concurrency spike from this tenant: concurrent_sessions ~= 280 (pool capacity is 320 for eu-west-2-tenant-17).

maya_ops: paging infra oncall — this looks like a hotpath for a single tenant. need fast mitigations: 1) soft throttle concurrency for tenant, 2) enable fallback to a smaller model variant to reduce token-CPU, 3) flush/evict KV cache for that tenant's pool.

infra-oncall: copy. prepared commands: 
- Set tenant concurrency cap:
```
redwoodctl tenant update-quotas --tenant heliospay --max-concurrency 8
```
- Enable fallback routing to 'gpt-lite-1' variant for pool:
```
redwoodctl routing set-fallback --pool eu-west-2-tenant-17 --model gpt-lite-1 --priority 10
```
- Evict tenant KV cache on pool nodes (rolling):
```
redwoodctl pool flush-kvcache --pool eu-west-2-tenant-17 --tenant heliospay
```
I'll run the concurrency cap and routing change now.

kai.chen: also suggest adding a short-term rate-limit on requests that contain long delimiter sequences — we can match via the request metadata. fallback can be safe-guarded.

eva-rl: adding a streaming-specific circuit breaker so streaming sessions > X seconds get preempted at the edge. We can push a config to the edge LB:
```
edgectl set-circuitbreaker --match 'delim_pattern' --max-stream-ms 5000
```
This will drop extremely long streams. need infra approval.

eng-sre-oncall: applied concurrency cap to heliospay -> 8. applied routing fallback to gpt-lite-1 with immediate priority. starting KV cache flush (rolling).

sasha.ng: after routing/fallback, p99 dropped to ~3.1s within two minutes. streaming stalls reduced. monitor still climbing on a few pods, likely draining.

incident-bot: Update: metric streaming.tail_latency.p99 = 2.9s (11:07:42 UTC). Incident severity downgraded to Sev-3.

maya_ops: infra noted elevated error rate for long-lived streams during KV flush. some sessions were reset — customer-facing sessions 0.6% aborted. Ops, please message CS.

infra-oncall: confirming flush caused ~120 TCP stream resets in the pool as nodes evicted caches and restarted tasks. mitigations: we can sequentially drain pods to reduce resets, but that will take longer. we opted for rolling flush which triggered resets.

kai.chen: still seeing unusual prefix distribution in logs — many prompts include repeating delimiter tokens that expand context window to >4k tokens. root cause hypothesis: customer-side prompt-generation bug that concatenates conversation with a delimiter every message leading to cache blowup. recommend asking customer to patch generator to use fewer delimiters or use streaming-chunks with shorter segmenting.

sasha.ng: assigned follow-up actions:
- @kai.chen to lead forensic logs + session replay (ETA 2h)
- @eva-rl to draft short-term edge circuit breaker PR and guardrail (ETA 1h)
- @maya_ops to notify CS and Customer Success on impact and mitigation steps (ETA 15m)
- infra to run a safer KV eviction plan for full recovery (ETA 30m)

eng-sre-oncall: handoff to infra-oncall for mitigation completion. I'll stay on call for the postmortem.

oncall-sre: taking ownership for the next hour. logging incident on-call-handovers channel.

maya_ops: CS notified customer — they acknowledged an internal change and will roll back the new prompt generator in an hour. they asked if we can keep the concurrency cap and fallback for 60min. approved.

eva-rl: quick note — once load normalizes, we should recommend model-quantization profile or stricter max-sequence default for single-tenant pools. will add to Optimize backlog.

sasha.ng: summary: immediate mitigations (cap + fallback + kvcache flush) reduced p99 from 12.4s -> 2.9s. customer impact ~0.6% aborted streams. follow-ups scheduled. moving thread to post-incident for timeline and RCA. :thumbsup:

kai.chen: adding logs + query examples to the forensic doc. will link once ready.

incident-bot: Incident note: started 1733332222, mitigations applied 1733332265, handoff 1733332360. Marking for postmortem.
